title: MELON: Provable Defense Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks in AI Agents
pdf_path: papers/MELON_Provable Defense Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks in AI Agents.pdf
threat_model_summary: Indirect prompt injection in tool outputs; MELON re-executes with a task-neutral prompt and compares tool calls against a cross-step cache. Detection is empirical; no cryptographic adversary model.
core_contributions: Masked re-execution detector for indirect prompt injection
Task-neutral prompt plus tool-output merging to reduce false positives/negatives
Cross-step tool-call cache and tool-call-only comparison
0.32% ASR and 68.72% utility on AgentDojo with GPT-4o (MELON-Aug)
limitations: 'Provable' refers only to a Hoeffding error bound for an ensemble detector not used in the main experiments
Depends on tool-call similarity and thresholds
theoretical_crypto_links: None; statistical error bound is not a cryptographic proof
applied_crypto_links: No encryption, signatures, credentials or TEE
Signed tool outputs are at most a peripheral provenance control

title: G-Safeguard: A Topology-Guided Security Lens and Treatment on LLM-based Multi-agent Systems
pdf_path: papers/G-Safeguard_A Topology-Guided Security Lens and Treatment on LLM-based Multi-agent Systems.pdf
threat_model_summary: Malicious or compromised agents in a multi-agent system; G-Safeguard builds a discourse graph and removes outgoing edges of detected high-risk agents after each round. Not a cryptographic adversary model.
core_contributions: Topology-guided security lens for LLM-MAS
Discourse graph with utterance embeddings and GAT node classification
Edge pruning to contain propagation
Evaluation across topologies, attacks and agent counts
limitations: Cannot prevent initial compromise, only contain spread
No formal guarantee; ASR defined as fraction of agents behaving maliciously
Some settings show ASR increases after defense
theoretical_crypto_links: None; graph topology is not authentication
Signed messages/agent credentials could improve attribution but not content safety (our inference)
applied_crypto_links: No encryption, signatures, MACs or credentials
Edge pruning is not access control

title: Position: Agent Security Needs Redefinition through a Holistic Framework
pdf_path: papers/Position_Agent Security Needs Redefinition through a Holistic Framework.pdf
threat_model_summary: Position paper arguing agent security should be defined by authorization context: source authorization, task alignment, action alignment and data isolation along a trajectory. No formal threat model or cryptographic adversary.
core_contributions: Authorization-context framing for agent security
Four properties: Source Authorization, Task Alignment, Action Alignment, Data Isolation
Reclassification of indirect/direct injection, task drift, capability misuse and cross-context leakage
Manual analysis of 45 AgentDojo/WASP injection tasks as motivating evidence
limitations: Position paper; no formal definitions, state machine or proof
Only 45 manual tasks as empirical basis
No model, dataset statistics, baseline or ablation
theoretical_crypto_links: None as written; provenance is source tracking, not cryptographic provenance
Signed task tokens/capabilities and provenance logs are our inference
applied_crypto_links: No encryption, signatures, credentials or TEE
Task/action alignment remains semantic; cryptography can bind scope but not judge intent

title: MINIM: Privacy-Aware Minimal View for Agents via Trusted Local Sanitization
pdf_path: papers/MINIM_Privacy-Aware Minimal View for Agents via Trusted Local Sanitization.pdf
threat_model_summary: Remote inference server is honest-but-curious; a trusted local broker sanitizes the UI accessibility tree before sending it. Local environment compromise, prompt injection and active attackers are explicitly out of scope.
core_contributions: Semantic over-privileged observation problem for UI agents
Local GATv2 broker predicting sensitivity and task necessity, then keep/abstract/remove
67.4% node reduction with high TCNP on WebArena-derived benchmark
Seven-LLM zero-shot comparison
limitations: Trusted local sanitization is a deployment assumption, not TEE/attestation
No formal privacy definition or leakage bound
No end-to-end agent task success evaluation
Annotator identity and split disjointness unclear
theoretical_crypto_links: None; mutual-information objective is not a cryptographic definition
TEE/remote attestation for the broker is our inference, not the paper's mechanism
applied_crypto_links: Broker attestation/signed policy could harden the local trust assumption (our inference)

title: Contextualized Privacy Defense for LLM Agents
pdf_path: papers/Contextualized Privacy Defense for LLM Agents.pdf
threat_model_summary: Three-agent simulation (data subject, data sender, data recipient) with privacy norms; CDI injects contextualized guidance before the sender acts. Not a cryptographic adversary model.
core_contributions: Contextualized Defense Instructing (CDI) for agent privacy
Formalizes prompting vs guarding as intervention points
GRPO training from failed trajectories with PP warm-up and AD optimization
100 unseen configurations: PP 94.2%, HS 80.6%, AD 86.5%
theoretical_crypto_links: None; contextual privacy is a normative/semantic notion
Formal information-flow/DP bounds are our inference
applied_crypto_links: No encryption, signatures, credentials or TEE
Cryptography cannot decide whether a disclosure is contextually appropriate
